sentences.text: The present Writ Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred against the arbitrary and unlawful inaction on the part of the Respondents in not acquiring the Petitioner's house despite it falling within the FTL Line of the Kundaliya Dam and getting directly affected by the same.

The said inaction of the Respondents has resulted in violation of fundamental rights of the Petitioner i.e. right to life and liberty as enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India and right against arbitrariness as enshrined under Article 14 of the Constitution of India.

That, the entire verification process, and multiple unnecessary rounds thereof, have been completed by the Respondents and the Petitioner has been repeatedly found to be directly affected by the Dam construction.

Respondent No. 7 himself has been writing to Respondents No. 2 and 4 pressing the urgency for proceeding with the acquisition process because of the impact of the Dam constriction on Petitioner's house.
Moreover, the Petitioner has already started facing sever flooding in his house starting from monsoon of 2023.

That, Respondent No. 2 (the District Collector) has already issued Form A under Madhya Pradesh Consented Land Purchase Policy, 2014 which lays out all the requisite specification of the land acquisition along with the rates being offered by the Government.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Consented Land Purchase Policy, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Petitioner has given his consent to the said Form A, by signing Form B as per the said policy.
Therefore, as per principles of law of contract, the process of offer and acceptance stand completed and an implied contract for purchase of the Petitioner's house by the Respondents is in force.

That,
despite several representations, the Respondents have not proceeded with the acquisition of the Petitioner's house and no compensation whatsoever has been paid to him.

Considering the approaching monsoon, the Petitioner is apprehensive of another round of flooding and in absence of compensation which may allow the Petitioner to find an alternate place of accommodation, the Petitioner is at sever risk of damage to person or property of the Petitioner and his family.

In view of the aforesaid submission, the present petition is disposed off with a direction to the respondent no.2/Collector to ventilate the grievance of the petitioners and to act upon as per the Annexure P/9.
The aforesaid exercise shall be carried out positively within the period of two months from the date of receipt of the order passed today.
The liberty is granted to the petitioner to claim interest, if he entitled in accordance with the law.
With the aforesaid the present petition stands disposed off.
